description: Test your knowledge of PA G1 | Cell Injury, Adaptation & Cell Death.

cards.text: Define pathology and explain its etymology.
cards.answer: Pathology is the scientific study of the structural, biochemical, and functional changes in cells, tissues, and organs that underlie disease. The word combines Greek roots: pathos (suffering) and logos (study).

tip.tip: Pathos = suffering; Logos = study — it's the study of what goes wrong in disease

cards.text: Name the four interconnected aspects through which every disease can be understood.
cards.answer: Etiology (cause), pathogenesis (mechanism), morphologic changes (structural alterations), and clinical significance (functional consequences and symptoms).

tip.tip: Remember EMMC: Etiology → Mechanism → Morphology → Clinical. They form a chain.

cards.text: Distinguish between etiology and pathogenesis. Why is this distinction clinically important?
cards.answer: Etiology is the cause of disease (e.g., infection, toxin); pathogenesis is the mechanism by which that cause produces disease (e.g., inflammation, cell death). Treatments may target either the cause or the mechanism.

tip.tip: Etiology = 'What caused it?' | Pathogenesis = 'How did it happen?'

cards.text: What are the two major domains of anatomic pathology? Give one example of each.
cards.answer: Surgical pathology (analyzing biopsy and resection specimens to confirm diagnosis, e.g., detecting malignancy) and cytopathology (examining individual cells, e.g., Pap smear, FNAC).

tip.tip: AP = Anatomy-based; you look at tissues and cells under the microscope

cards.text: State Virchow's landmark principle (1858) and its significance in pathology.
cards.answer: 'Omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells arise from cells) established the cell as the fundamental unit of disease and founded modern cellular pathology, replacing humoral theory.

tip.tip: Virchow's cellular revolution: the cell is the foundation of all pathology

cards.text: Define the terms lesion, morbidity, and mortality in pathological context.
cards.answer: Lesion = any pathological structural change in tissue. Morbidity = the extent or burden of disease in a population. Mortality = the death rate in a population.

tip.tip: Lesion = damage; Morbidity = disease load; Mortality = death count

cards.text: Describe the cell cycle phases and explain why proliferative capacity matters for regeneration.
cards.answer: G1 (growth/preparation), S (DNA synthesis), G2 (pre-mitotic checkpoint), M (mitosis); G0 = quiescent. Regeneration depends on a tissue's ability to re-enter the cycle from G0 and proliferate to replace damaged cells.

tip.tip: G = Gap (growth), S = Synthesis, M = Mitosis; G0 = resting but can be reactivated

cards.text: What is iatrogenic disease and why is it important in clinical pathology?
cards.answer: Iatrogenic disease is disease caused by medical treatment (e.g., drug toxicity, surgical complications). It is important because the pathologist must recognize treatment-related changes and distinguish them from disease progression.

tip.tip: Iatrogenic = doctor-induced (iatros = physician); always consider in post-treatment biopsies
